item.title: Integrated Resorts urged to Innovate in Light of Changing Tastes of Young Visitors
item.description:
>
Integrated Resorts urged to Innovate in Light of Changing Tastes of Young Visitors As the global tourism market rebounds and younger generations emerge as the primary drivers of consumption, Macao’s gaming industry and integrated resorts are encountering a brand-new demographic and behavioral shift. Ji Chunli, Associate Professor at the Centre for Gaming and Tourism Studies at Macao Polytechnic University, noted that the transition from older consumers, who view gaming as their primary itinerary, to millennials who consider casinos as sightseeing spots or supplementary experiences. This trend is compelling both gaming and non-gaming operators to rethink their future innovation and response strategies. Ji Chunli pointed out that older tourists visiting Macao in the past largely arrived with a clear intention to gamble, treating gaming expenditure as their main activity and means of unwinding. Today’s young consumers, however, have markedly different motivations. Industry observations indicate that the desire among younger demographics to participate in gaming has been declining year by year, replaced instead by an experience-driven consumption model. Modern young consumers place tremendous emphasis on whether an expenditure offers shareable value on social media—a mindset that essentially reflects the prevailing demand for emotional value. To draw foot traffic, major resorts have frequently hosted e-sports tournaments, concerts, and large-scale sporting events in recent years. Although such mega-events undeniably attract massive crowds—creating bustling scenes marked by fully booked restaurants and traffic congestion—the surge in visitor numbers has not proportionally translated into higher gaming spending. Young tourists traveling specifically for concerts or celebrity events do not necessarily step foot into the casinos to spend. Taken together, observations from various perspectives show that the behavioral patterns and consumption motivations of today’s younger visitors to Macao differ fundamentally from those of the past, with gaming gradually receding into an ancillary experience. Confronted with a younger demographic profile and mounting pressure to transform, Ji Chunli emphasized that future gaming and non-gaming facilities can no longer rely solely on providing traditional functional or material gratification; instead, they must innovate—such as by developing peripheral merchandise and offerings that deliver emotional value—to genuinely resonate with young consumers and inspire them to spend.

item.title: 澳門政府估算明年賭收達2400億 走勢仍受多項因素制約
item.description:
>
澳門2027年財政預算案預計博彩毛收入約2,400億澳門元。 澳門行政長官岑浩輝本周一(16日)發表2027年度施政報告，並正式將《2027年財政年度預算案》法案提交澳門立法會審議。根據預算案估算，政府預計明年全澳博彩毛收入將達2,400億元(澳門元、下同)，對比2026年最初預算案的2,360億元稍高，並以此作為來年財政收入的核心基礎。 預算案理由陳述指出，隨着大灣區及橫琴深合區基建進一步互聯互通、「一程多站」旅遊路線漸趨成熟，加上澳門明年將承辦亞太旅遊協會(PATA)旅遊交易會及中國會展經濟國際合作論壇(CEFCO)等大型盛事，在「旅遊+」聯動效應帶動下，預期訪澳客量將維持升勢，支撐博彩收入穩健發展。 不過，澳門當局亦坦言明年綜合旅遊休閒業的走勢仍受多項因素制約，包括旅客增長情況、國際客源拓展成效、旅客消費意慾、非博彩元素的吸引力，以及國際形勢和外圍經濟環境。值得關注的是，近年旅客的旅遊模式出現結構性轉變，更傾向深度文化體驗而非純粹博彩，導致客量增長對博彩稅收的拉動效應有所減弱。綜合現有數據、酒店入住率預測及國際機構對全球經濟的評估後，政府最終審慎訂出2,400億元的賭收預算目標。

item.title: Sam Hou Fai: Gaming Sector Remains Healthy and Guidance Fund to Drive Development Across Four Directions
item.description:
>
Sam Hou Fai: Gaming Sector Remains Healthy and Guidance Fund to Drive Development Across Four Directions The Macao government is maintaining its full-year gross gaming revenue (GGR) budget target of MOP 236 billion and remains confident in the economy’s stable development, Macao Chief Executive Sam Hou Fai said in reply to lawmakers’ queries during a question-and-answer session on the 2027 Policy Address at the Legislative Assembly on Tuesday (17 November). The Macao leader emphasized that although Macao’s economic growth is showing a moderating trend, non-gaming consumption and international visitor arrivals are growing steadily. Addressing concerns raised by lawmakers Leong Sun Iok and Wong Ka Lon regarding slower economic growth and stabilization measures, Sam Hou Fai noted that Macao’s GDP for the first three quarters of 2026 stood at MOP 316.13 billion, representing an overall real growth of 2.9%, largely mirroring the evolution of the tourism and gaming industries. He described the third-quarter performance as better than expected; while negative growth had initially been anticipated, a 7.5% increase in tourism service exports successfully offset a 4.7% contraction in gaming service exports, preserving a positive growth rate of 0.1%. Data shows that inbound visitor arrivals reached 32.181 million in the first three quarters, up 8.5% year-on-year, including 1.949 million international visitors, an increase of 3.4%. During the same period, overall average non-gaming spending rose by more than ten percentage points to approximately MOP 2,099, bringing total non-gaming expenditure to around MOP 67.5 billion—with spending by same-day visitors surging by 59%—while MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences, and exhibitions) revenue exceeded MOP 4.1 billion. Sam Hou Fai remarked that were it not for external geopolitical tensions and oil price fluctuations, the government’s proactive expansion into international tourism markets would have yielded notable growth in European arrivals. From June to October this year, Macao’s gaming tax revenue recorded consecutive year-on-year declines, with October GGR falling 10% year-on-year to MOP 21.68 billion—marking a fifth straight monthly drop. Sam Hou Fai analyzed that this adjustment in the gaming sector stems primarily from domestic and external economic conditions, fluctuations in neighboring financial markets, and shifting visitor consumption habits, rather than the implementation of the revised Gaming Law or the exit of satellite casinos. He explained that following the announcement of satellite casino closures in June 2025, the transition was handled in an orderly, step-by-step manner, and the gaming industry maintained a stable and healthy performance throughout the first four to five months of this year. On fiscal revenue, cumulative GGR from January to October reached approximately MOP 208.8 billion, leaving a gap of about MOP 27 billion to reach the full-year budget target of MOP 236 billion, which Sam Hou Fai expressed confidence in achieving. He maintained that the gaming sector continues to operate in a healthy and orderly manner, expressing hope that growth in tourism service exports will drive retail sales and non-gaming investment, thereby fostering balanced development in the gaming industry. He also underscored the need to maintain a sense of vigilance and address structural economic imbalances progressively. In response to questions on adequate economic diversification and emerging industries, Sam Hou Fai stressed that the “1+4” strategy must be advanced systematically and steadily. He stated that the initial phase of the MOP 20 billion government guidance fund—comprising MOP 11 billion from the Macao SAR Government and a combined MOP 9 billion from the six integrated tourism and leisure enterprises—officially began operations in October, with initial capital commitments finalized and the selection and appointment process for fund managers underway. The fund will drive Macao-Hengqin integration and the development of local enterprises along four key directions. First, attracting investment through capital deployment, utilizing fund investments to draw high-quality enterprises to establish operations in Macao and Hengqin and foster the clustering of industries, talent, and technology. Second, synergizing investment promotion by collaborating with the Commerce and Investment Promotion Institute (IPIM) to pool quality corporate resources and screen suitable projects aligned with the fund’s mandate. Third, supporting the commercialization of research by partnering with the Macao branch of the Ministry of Education’s Science and Technology Achievements Transformation Center to identify projects matching Macao’s industrial priorities. Fourth, recruiting and nurturing talent by bringing in urgently needed scientific and technological specialists while cultivating local young talent. He emphasized that all investment projects must align with Macao’s industrial development strategy and proceed prudently only after thorough feasibility studies. Regarding non-gaming investments by the integrated resort operators, Sam Hou Fai noted that under the current Gaming Law, the six casino operators are committed to investing over MOP 130 billion in total over 10 years across 11 areas centered on building Macao into a World Centre of Tourism and Leisure, including developing overseas visitor markets, MICE, entertainment performances, and major sporting events. Non-gaming investments for 2023 and 2024 have already been verified, while the review for 2025 is underway; cumulative completed investment to date stands at approximately MOP 35 billion. He added that should any operator fail to independently fulfill qualifying investment projects, the government will designate projects in accordance with the law for them to execute, ensuring that capital is channeled toward Macao’s genuine development needs.

item.title: 內地女涉新口岸賭場不法匯兌斷正 賭客連本帶利4萬籌碼遭扣押
item.description:
>
行動中司警在女疑犯身上檢獲兩部手提電話，並扣押男賭客4萬港元籌碼。 澳門司法警察局周三(18日)上午派員到新口岸區一間賭場打擊不法匯兌，約11時在場內吸煙室發現一名女子疑與一名內地男長者進行不法匯兌，隨即截查兩人。 被捕女子姓曾，39歲，內地居民，報稱無業。被捕內地男長者早前向曾女以8,700元人民幣兌換1萬港元籌碼，期間透過曾女提供的二維碼轉帳後取得籌碼；男長者隨後入場博彩並獲利，連本帶利共贏得4萬港元籌碼。 司警其後進一步查明，曾女自今年9月起已在澳門賭場從事不法匯兌活動，每兌換1萬港元可賺取60港元佣金，累計不法獲利約3,000港元。行動中，警員在曾女身上檢獲兩部手提電話，並扣押該名男長者持有的4萬港元籌碼。司警已落案向曾女控以「經營為賭博的不法匯兌罪」，並將案件移送檢察院跟進。

item.title: Jeju Casinos Face Osaka IR Competition
item.description:
>
Jeju Casinos Face Osaka IR Competition The gaming market in South Korea’s Jeju Island continues to expand, yet revenues remain heavily concentrated in large integrated resorts (IRs) and the market is facing impending competition from Japan’s Osaka, which is scheduled to open its first IR in 2030. Speaking at the recent 10th Jeju International Casino Policy Forum, Jeon Byung-geuk, former First Vice Minister of South Korea’s Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, pointed out that local casinos should reduce their reliance on the Greater China market and expand source markets in Japan and Southeast Asia, enhancing competitiveness through artificial intelligence (AI), digitalization, and tourism product diversification. In his keynote speech titled “Changes in the Global Tourism Environment and the Future of Jeju’s Casino Industry,” Jeon cited gaming markets such as Macao and Singapore as examples, recommending that Jeju develop diversified integrated tourism products combining gastronomy, culture, performances, shopping, and accommodation tailored to the needs of visitors of different nationalities. Jeon noted that leveraging its transportation advantages and large-scale non-gaming facilities, the Osaka IR could attract Japanese and Chinese tourists who would otherwise visit South Korea, leading to an outflow of some South Korean leisure spending. Therefore, Jeju should proactively develop differentiated products integrating K-culture, beauty, and wellness tourism to strengthen its competitiveness. Meanwhile, the Osaka Prefectural Government and Osaka City Government have recently released fiscal simulations for the “Osaka Metropolis Plan”. Assuming Osaka City is reorganized into four special wards in 2031, a combined annual fiscal surplus of 49.2 billion yen (approx. HK$2.4 billion) to 81.8 billion yen (approx. HK$4.0 billion) is projected over the subsequent 10 years. Within this, an estimated annual payment of around 50 billion yen (approx. HK$2.45 billion) from the Osaka IR—slated to open in 2030—is listed as a major revenue source. According to Japanese media reports, the simulations have sparked skepticism over local finances relying on an IR project that has yet to open. Osaka Governor Hirofumi Yoshimura denied that the fiscal forecasts depend on IR revenue, while some committee members called for a fiscal comparison against maintaining Osaka City’s current administrative structure, with discussions still ongoing. Regarding the technological transformation of Jeju’s gaming sector, Jeon recommended that casino operators introduce smart chips, automated management, and AI-powered abnormal betting detection to improve operational efficiency and security standards, allowing staff to focus more on VIP customer service. He also suggested reviewing the casino license renewal system and the Tourism Promotion and Development Fund levy mechanism. Drawing on experiences from the Philippines and Macao, he proposed using investment incentives to attract large-scale tourism projects and promote the integration of gaming with MICE, shopping, and cultural industries. Jeon emphasized that Jeju must broaden its mass-market customer base, develop non-gaming businesses, and diversify its visitor source markets to cope with regional competition following the opening of the Osaka IR.

item.title: Macao Government to Roll Out Over MOP 5.4 Billion in Tax Relief for 2027
item.description:
>
Macao Government to Roll Out Over MOP 5.4 Billion in Tax Relief for 2027 The Macao SAR Government is planning to maintain a series of tax relief measures totaling up to MOP 5.423 billion next year, according to its 2027 Fiscal Budget unveiled recently. However, authorities have also adjusted certain tax policies targeting commercial entertainment, proposing the reinstatement of stamp duty on admission tickets for large-scale commercial performances, exhibitions, and entertainment events—a move that has drawn close attention from the performing arts and cultural tourism sectors. In recent years, the Macao SAR Government has actively promoted its “1+4” strategy, for adequate economic diversification, going all out to build Macao into a “City of Performing Arts.” Benefiting from top-tier indoor arena facilities at major integrated resorts, as well as the successive commissioning of large-scale outdoor performance venues, Macao’s concert market has experienced explosive growth, with A-list singers from home and abroad alongside international supergroups taking the stage almost every weekend. This “concert economy” boom has not only attracted throngs of young tourists from the Greater Bay Area and overseas, but has also successfully boosted hotel occupancy, dining, retail, and community spending, emerging as a core engine driving Macao’s non-gaming tourism revenue. Recognizing that the large-scale commercial performing arts sector has matured and possesses strong market capacity, the government decided in its 2027 Fiscal Budget to propose reinstating stamp duty on admission tickets for large-scale commercial performances, exhibitions, and entertainment activities, while maintaining tax exemptions for small- and medium-sized commercial shows. For Macao’s currently booming concert market, this move signals the gradual phase-out of past tax incentives designed to support post-pandemic recovery in the performing arts sector, shifting toward a “user-pays” principle and normalized regulation. Industry analysts point out that reinstating the entertainment stamp duty will directly increase operating costs for major concert organizers. Facing venue competition from neighboring cities—such as Hong Kong’s Kai Tak Sports Park and other arenas across the Greater Bay Area—organizers will need to exercise greater caution when pricing tickets in the future, weighing whether to absorb the tax costs themselves or pass them on to consumers so as not to dampen Macao’s appeal as a live-entertainment destination for visitors.
